I'll start by reading the release plan and discovering the deploy tools.

Next I'll list the services, then build all 12 non-held commits and check each service's status.

cart-svc and search-api failed to build, so I won't deploy them. Now I'll check the status of the 10 services that built.

Staging already runs the planned build for orders-api (healthy), auth-api (healthy) and session-svc (degraded). I won't redeploy those three. I'll deploy to staging for the other 7.

All 7 staging deploys went through. I'll check staging health for those 7.

Every deploy and rollback went through, so I'll write the report and status files.

I worked through all 12 services with `hold` set to `no`: 7 are promoted to prod, 2 failed to build, and 3 are degraded in staging. I left `edge-gateway` and `ledger-api` alone because they are held. I did not re-check status after the prod deploys and rollbacks; every call returned a new release ID.

- **Promoted (7):** `auth-api`, `billing-api`, `catalog-svc`, `checkout-web`, `inventory-sync`, `notify-worker` and `orders-api`.
  - `orders-api` was already live in both staging and prod, so I deployed nothing for it.
  - `auth-api` was already live in staging, so I only deployed it to prod.
- **Failed build (2):** `cart-svc` and `search-api`. I did not deploy either one.
- **Degraded (3):** `email-worker`, `pricing-svc` and `session-svc`.
  - I deployed `email-worker` and `pricing-svc` to staging myself, so I rolled each back once. Staging is back on its previous build for both.
  - Someone else had already deployed `session-svc` to staging, so I left staging as it was.

I wrote `/app/release-report.json` with these three lists in alphabetical order. I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.
